domain_restrictions: n and r must be integers.
The inequality 0 <= r <= n is required.
The quantity n - r is therefore a nonnegative integer.
The product defining (q;q)_m uses m as a nonnegative integer.
The claim is about a polynomial in the indeterminate q with coefficients in the integers.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every pair of integers n and r satisfying 0 <= r <= n, the expression (q;q)_n divided by the product of (q;q)_r and (q;q)_{n-r} is a well-defined nonzero polynomial in Z[q], and its degree as a polynomial in q is r times (n - r).
quantifier_order: For all integers n and r, if 0 <= r <= n, then the stated property holds for the polynomial in q defined by the given formula.

statement_nl: For all integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient [n choose r]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}), where (q;q)_m := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^i) and (q;q)_0 := 1, is a nonzero polynomial in Z[q] of degree r(n-r).
